rationale: Vortioxetine (SMS; t½ ~66h; multimodal serotonergic; low discontinuation syndrome risk due to long half-life) to escitalopram (SSRI). Vortioxetine's very long half-life provides a natural pharmacokinetic self-taper — plasma levels fall gradually over ~2 weeks after stopping. This substantially reduces discontinuation syndrome risk. A direct switch or minimal overlap approach is clinically reasonable. Both agents are serotonergic — brief overlap may cause mild additive serotonergic effects but serotonin syndrome risk is low at standard doses. Start escitalopram at full therapeutic dose from day 1 of the switch. No CYP2D6 interaction: escitalopram is not a CYP2D6 inhibitor (unlike fluoxetine/paroxetine which would require vortioxetine dose adjustment). PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

schedule.notes: Stop vortioxetine. Start escitalopram 10 mg. Vortioxetine's long half-life (66h) means levels fall gradually — no discontinuation syndrome expected. Brief overlap for clinical safety. Escitalopram has no CYP2D6 inhibition — no dose adjustment needed for vortioxetine residual levels during washout.
Vortioxetine now fully cleared. Continue escitalopram 10 mg. Titrate to 20 mg at 4 weeks if response inadequate.

doseRatios.equivalencyNote: Vortioxetine 20 mg → escitalopram 10 mg (standard effective doses). Not pharmacologically equivalent. PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.
